cases.headline: A clearer account structure for a multi-specialty clinic.
cases.secondaryMetric: SAR 7.26 per recorded conversion · July 1 to 25, 2026 · SAR 5,906.11 spend
cases.challenge: A multi-specialty clinic account needed a clearer structure and more reliable measurement for each goal.
cases.solution: Separated campaigns by specialty and city, redefined primary conversions and adjusted bidding to the value of each objective.
cases.finePrint: Recorded conversions are not necessarily confirmed patient bookings.
cases.context: Google Ads recorded conversions during a 25-day reporting window. They may include multiple conversion actions and are not the same as confirmed medical bookings. The account held steady while it scaled: 464 conversions at SAR 4.03 at launch, 681 at SAR 7.63 in June, then 814 at SAR 7.26 in July.
cases.summary: Campaigns organized by specialty and city, with measurement aligned to each objective.

proofs.caption: Google Ads campaigns, July 1 to 25, 2026: 814 conversions at SAR 7.26. Campaign names blurred.
June 2026 account summary: 681 conversions at SAR 7.63.
Launch period, May 20 to June 15, 2026: 464 conversions at SAR 4.03, 15.97% conversion rate.

cases.headline: Patient enquiries through WhatsApp and Messenger.
cases.secondaryMetric: SAR 3.72 to 3.83 per lead · June 1 to 22, 2026 · SAR 2,281 spend
cases.challenge: The same clinic needed a second, lower-cost source of patient enquiries alongside Google Search.
cases.solution: Ran click-to-message campaigns on Facebook and Instagram that open a chat with the clinic's team, alongside the Google Ads account.
cases.finePrint: Each lead is a new patient enquiry by chat, not yet a confirmed booking.
cases.context: Leads counted as new WhatsApp and Messenger conversations, as reported by Meta Ads across two lead campaigns (229 and 373) over 22 days. Each lead is a person who contacted the clinic. It is not the same as a booked appointment.
cases.summary: Lead campaigns on Facebook and Instagram that bring patients into a chat with the clinic, at under SAR 4 per lead.

proofs.caption: Meta Ads, June 1 to 22, 2026: 229 + 373 messaging conversations at SAR 3.72 and SAR 3.83. Campaign names blurred.

cases.headline: Turning purchase intent into reported sales.
cases.secondaryMetric: ≈SAR 103K purchase value on SAR 11.8K spend · February 1 to March 24, 2026
cases.challenge: A travel-bag store was receiving low-quality paid traffic.
cases.solution: Isolated purchase-intent search terms in Exact Match, built negative keyword lists and improved the product and checkout journey.
cases.finePrint: Reported advertising return is not net profit.
cases.context: Purchase value reported by Google Ads, divided by cost for the same period. For comparison, the store backend recorded SAR 103.7K in sales from 234 orders between February 3 and March 5, across all channels, so not every order came from Google Ads. Return on ad spend is not net profit.
cases.summary: Focused search campaigns and a clearer journey from product page to checkout.

proofs.caption: Google Ads, February 1 to March 24, 2026: about SAR 103K purchase value on SAR 11.8K cost.
Store backend (Salla), February 3 to March 5, 2026: SAR 103.7K sales from 234 orders, all channels.

cases.headline: Website sales in a European market.
cases.secondaryMetric: ≈NOK 47,000 spend · July 1 to October 15, 2026 · best campaign: 69 purchases at NOK 216.95
cases.challenge: A Norwegian online store needed Meta Ads to bring in website purchases, not just traffic.
cases.solution: Purchase-optimized campaigns on Facebook and Instagram, with budget moved toward the campaigns with the lowest cost per purchase.
cases.finePrint: Purchases are attributed by Meta Ads and are not net profit.
cases.context: Website purchases reported by Meta Ads, summed across the campaigns shown. In August alone the account recorded 71 purchases on NOK 14,686.73, and the store's own report showed NOK 47,079.70 in sales that month, up 261.5% on July across all channels.
cases.summary: Purchase-focused Facebook and Instagram campaigns for a store in Norway.

proofs.caption: Meta Ads, July 1 to October 15, 2026: website purchases by campaign. Campaign names blurred.
August 2026: 71 website purchases on NOK 14,686.73 spend.

cases.headline: Steady website sales from Meta Ads.
cases.secondaryMetric: SAR 120.75 per purchase · January 1 to April 21, 2026 · SAR 19,682.11 spend
cases.challenge: An online store in Saudi Arabia needed paid social to produce purchases it could track, not just engagement.
cases.solution: Conversion campaigns optimized for website purchases and measured through the Meta Pixel.
cases.finePrint: Cost per purchase is not profit. Order value varies by product.
cases.context: Website purchases attributed by Meta Ads. Delivery was paused for most of February, so the total covers roughly three months of active campaigns.
cases.summary: Conversion campaigns for an online store, measured by website purchases.

proofs.caption: Meta Ads, January 1 to April 21, 2026: 163 website purchases at SAR 120.75 each.

cases.headline: Leads at volume, at a low cost.
cases.secondaryMetric: Two accounts · ≈$3,560 spend · September 1 to October 15, 2026 · from $0.31 per lead
cases.challenge: Two businesses that sell through chat needed a steady flow of new leads at a cost they could sustain.
cases.solution: Lead generation campaigns that open a WhatsApp or Messenger chat, with daily budgets scaled through the ad sets that delivered the lowest cost per lead.
cases.finePrint: Each lead is a new enquiry by chat, not yet a sale.
cases.context: Leads counted as new messaging conversations reported by Meta Ads. Account A: 2,126 leads on about $1,085 (September 15 to October 14). Account B: 1,944 leads on $2,474.89 (September 1 to October 15). The best campaign reached $0.31 per lead.
cases.summary: Lead campaigns across two accounts, averaging under $1 per lead.

proofs.caption: Account A, September 15 to October 14, 2026: 581 + 499 + 1,046 conversations on about $1,085.
Account B, September 1 to October 15, 2026: 1,944 conversations on $2,474.89.
